decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding correctly classify this paper as a replication: the authors collected new eye-tracking and learning performance data in an adolescent prevocational sample to re-test the findings of their prior published study. Prior attempts failed quote validation because they reconstructed interleaved two-column text instead of preserving the literal contiguous source text.

decisions.reason: With the target original resolved to Van Wermeskerken & Van Gog (2017), the authors state an explicit overall verdict that they replicated their previous findings: seeing the model's face reduced relative dwell time on the task area without affecting performance on either the molecule-building test or the knowledge test. Because both the attentional effect and the null learning effect match the findings of Van Wermeskerken & Van Gog (2017), the replication outcome is successful, whereas shipped 'mixed' reflected either a misreading of the null learning effect or comparison against the wrong chain source (Van Gog et al., 2014).
